note: Expected values were derived by Contracts/fixtures/derive-expected-values.py, a third implementation independent of both SDKs. Two SDKs agreeing with each other would prove nothing; agreeing with an outside implementation is the actual evidence.
signatureNote: Every proof value in this directory was signed by derive-expected-values.py with the test keypair and an RFC 6979 deterministic nonce, so the files reproduce byte for byte. A platform signer draws a random nonce, so its proofs are judged by verification against the test public key rather than byte equality.

testKeyPair.note: TEST KEYPAIR ONLY — NOT A SECRET. The keypair is restated byte for byte from SPFN primitives __tests__/test-keys.ts, where publishing the private half is intentional. It authenticates nothing, was never issued by anything, and must never be presented to a real endpoint.

vectors.name: handshake-no-body
vectors.why: an operation with no body carries the absent-body digest, not the digest of an empty string

vectors.name: echo-with-canonical-body
vectors.why: bodySha256 is taken over the canonical body, so it is stable across key order

vectors.name: unicode-in-nonce
vectors.why: proof input is UTF-8, so a non-ASCII nonce must not change length semantics

signatureRejects.name: der-encoded
signatureRejects.why: the same signature that verifies as raw r||s must be refused in DER; a platform signer that emits DER converts before sending, never the verifier

signatureRejects.name: uppercase-hex
signatureRejects.why: the wire encoding is base16-lower; an uppercase digest is a different string

signatureRejects.name: truncated-63-bytes
signatureRejects.why: a raw signature is exactly 64 bytes; 126 hex characters is not one

signatureRejects.name: not-hex
signatureRejects.why: 128 characters that are not all hex digits never reach the curve

signatureRejects.name: wrong-key
signatureRejects.why: a well-formed signature by another key must fail verification, not formatting

signatureRejects.name: all-zero
signatureRejects.why: r = s = 0 is outside [1, n-1] and can never verify
